headline: Why Do My New Cabinets Look Uneven?
articleBody: It's a frustrating moment when you step back to admire your newly installed kitchen cabinets, only to notice they're not quite level or aligned. This often happens because of a few common oversights during installation. First, failing to verify that walls and floors are perfectly level and plumb before installation is a big one. Even a slight imperfection can throw off the entire cabinet run, leading to misaligned doors, uneven gaps, and major problems when it's time to install countertops. Another mistake is rushing the assembly or installation process, not shimming cabinets correctly, or failing to fasten them securely to wall studs. Cheap hardware or flimsy box construction can also contribute to issues down the line, making doors and drawers sag or go out of alignment quickly. Finally, inadequate planning of the layout, like poor appliance clearances, can lead to awkward spacing that makes the whole kitchen feel off-kilter. To avoid these issues, it's really important to take your time and, if you're not experienced, to bring in professionals.
